transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Evan Park (CTO - SilverGrove), Maya Lin (Engineering Manager), Carlos Torres (DevOps), Olivia Grant (Data Ops)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Kickoff/check-in to align on staging access, network requirements, and initial runbook.
- Confirmed Redwood will share runbook draft and staging checklist; Redwood to provision an eval cluster and VPN instructions; customer to share sample prompts and data export.
- Discussed VPC routing, KMS options, and minimal latency targets.

Topics:
- Access & credentials (VPN, IAM, static IP)
- Network & firewall (egress/ingress rules)
- Staging cluster provisioning and runbook next steps
- Observability/tracing and cost guardrails
- Timeline for pilot (2-3 weeks target)

Action items (captured in notes): see metadata action_items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — good morning. Quick check, can folks hear me ok?
[00:06] Evan (SilverGrove): Yep yep, good here.
[00:08] Maya: Good morning.
[00:10] Priya (Redwood SE): Morning all, Priya here. I pulled up the onboarding runbook template in case we want to walk through sections.
[00:18] Carlos: I can see your screen, faint echo but fine. We're on SF time so, uh, thanks for coordinating.
[00:25] Jamie: Awesome. Goal for today is a short standup: confirm access method for staging, who owns firewall rules, and we timebox the pilot kickoff.
[00:34] Evan: Sounds good. We're generally leaning private VPC for now, at least for pilot. Compliance wants logs retained for 90 days and key management via our KMS.
[00:43] Jamie: Perfect — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated. For hosted we do envelope encryption but sometimes customers prefer their own KMS.
[00:52] Maya: Quick Q — what's the minimal network config? We want to minimize infra churn.
[00:56] Priya: Minimal is: outbound HTTPS to Redwood control plane for metrics, plus inbound only from the staging bastion to the cluster if we're doing private. For Dedicated we'd ask for static egress or allowlist IPs.
[01:10] Olivia: And for data egress — do tokens or logs leave our VPC by default? Need to confirm with security.
[01:16] Jamie: Good point. By default in Private deployment nothing leaves customer VPC except returns from model inference. Metrics can be pushed via a forwarder; we can also run the forwarding collector inside their network. So it can be airtight.
[01:31] Carlos: Ok, so concretely, we'll need an allowlist of IPs and a route to the Redwood control endpoints. I'll take ownership of firewall rules but need the list.
[01:38] Priya: I'll attach the allowlist in the onboarding doc — note sometimes the IPs differ by region, we'll call out the region mapping.
[01:45] Evan: Timeline — we want a pilot in two weeks if possible. Are we realistic on that?
[01:49] Jamie: Two weeks is aggressive but doable for a proof-of-concept if data handoff is quick and we do staging only. We'll scope minimal success criteria: 1) full inference path for 1-2 demo flows, 2) latency under X ms — what do you want to target?
[02:04] Maya: Ideally p95 under 280ms for our 256-token typical prompt. If that's unrealistic, we can accept a higher p95 for pilot.
[02:11] Priya: We'll baseline on the model variant you plan to use. For cost/latency trade-offs we can suggest a quantized variant for pilot. Small caveat: quantization sometimes affects outputs for few specialized prompts.
[02:25] Olivia: We do have a couple of hallucination-sensitive prompt sets; quantify tradeoffs please.
[02:29] Jamie: Yes, we'll run a quality regression on your sample prompts — please send them. That leads to the first action: customer to share prompt set and a small dataset export.
[02:39] Evan: Noted. We'll share by end of week.
[02:42] Carlos: For the staging cluster — do you provision the GPU nodes or we spin up an infra template?
[02:48] Priya: For private/Dedicated we provide a deployment manifest and recommended instance types; we can also do a short-lived eval cluster for you if you want Redwood-managed staging. Jamie?
[02:57] Jamie: We can offer a managed eval cluster for the pilot window — reduces friction. It will still require VPN tunnel/peering and IAM rules. If you prefer to self-host, Priya will provide Terraform and deployment docs.
[03:08] Maya: Managed eval is appealing to our PMs. Could be faster. How about credentials and access — SSO?
[03:14] Jamie: We support SAML SSO for Console access; for cluster-level access we'll give short-lived certs and can integrate with your IdP. For the eval cluster we'll hand off a service account plus a jump host.
[03:27] Carlos: Okay. For security review, our compliance team will want SOC2 and data flow diagrams. Do you have those ready?
[03:33] Jamie: Yes — I'll send the SOC 2 summary and a high-level architecture diagram. Full security package is in the security pack link I'll share post-call.
[03:40] Evan: Great. Also curious about observability — we want per-route token cost and end-to-end latency traces.
[03:46] Priya: The Console exposes token-level breakdowns and traces. For private deployments you can forward spans to your tracing backend (we support Jaeger/OTEL). We'll show an example in the observability deep-dive.
[03:58] Olivia: Nice. For billing — who gets billed for the eval cluster? We need to know if costs run through our cloud account or Redwood's trial pool.
[04:05] Jamie: Managed eval is covered by Redwood trial credits for a short period; production Dedicated will be invoiced to your account. We'll capture budget guardrails in the runbook.
[04:16] Evan: Ok. A couple of nitty-gritty: does Redwood require persistent KV cache in the cluster or is that ephemeral?
[04:22] Priya: KV cache is ephemeral by default; it's process-local per node. For session warm-starting we rely on prefix caching. If you need durable caching we can outline a strategy but it's not typical for pilot.
[04:34] Maya: Another ask — can we limit token generation rates per route? We want to safeguard against runaway usage.
[04:39] Jamie: Yes, you can configure per-route rate limits and cost thresholds. We'll add recommended defaults to the runbook.
[04:48] Carlos: Network question: static IPs for outbound, is that available in managed eval?
[04:53] Priya: Managed eval may have a small pool of egress IPs; we can provide them but if you need guaranteed static IPs in your account, self-hosted in your VPC is the way.
[05:03] Evan: For the pilot acceptance criteria — let's capture it: specific flows working, p95 under 350ms perhaps for first milestone, and no PII exfiltration in logs.
[05:12] Jamie: Sounds reasonable. We'll draft the acceptance checklist and share.
[05:16] -- brief pause as Jamie shares a doc --
[05:30] [06:00] Priya: I'm posting a link to the onboarding runbook in chat (link: internal/runbook-sg). It's the template we'll populate.
[06:04] Maya: Got it, seeing it.
[06:06] Carlos: I'll need the allowlist and the list of control-plane endpoints; can you put both in the doc?
[06:11] Priya: Will do. Also attaching a sample Terraform snippet for the cluster.
[06:17] Olivia: For data retention, we want encryption at rest with our KMS. You mentioned support earlier — is there any limitation?
[06:23] Jamie: No limitation — we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated. For hosted, you can bring keys in some enterprise plans; we'll clarify in the security pack.
[06:33] Evan: Any blockers on our side to get started?
[06:36] Carlos: I'll need a list of required firewall ports and the static IPs, and a small manifest for allowed DNS names. Also need an IAM role spec for the service account.
[06:46] Jamie: We'll include all of that in the runbook. I'll mark the firewall list as high priority.
[06:50] Maya: Do we need to schedule a canary rollout or A/B test session?
[06:55] Priya: For pilot we recommend a canary path — route X% of traffic to Redwood variant so you can test quality. We can automate rollback based on quality/regression alerts.
[07:06] Olivia: That would be helpful. How are regression alerts defined?
[07:10] Priya: Alerts are tied to prompt sets and evals — you can set a threshold on metrics like ROUGE or custom scoring. If quality drops beyond threshold, we trigger a rollback or notify stakeholders.
[07:22] Evan: Are there any special licensing or compliance forms we need to sign before eval cluster spin-up?
[07:27] Jamie: Standard NDA/PSA are covered; I'll follow up with a link to the PO and any MSA samples. For the pilot we normally operate under an evaluation agreement — I'll attach.
[07:37] Carlos: From infra perspective, timeline: I can stand up the peering and basic firewall changes in 48 hours once you send the IPs.
[07:44] Jamie: Great. So let's capture owners: Jamie sends runbook + security pack; Priya provisions deployment docs and egress allowlist; Carlos to complete firewall work; Evan to share samples.
[07:55] Maya: Quick note — we have a compliance meeting next Wed; would be good to have the security pack by Monday.
[08:01] Jamie: Ok I will aim to send the security pack and runbook draft by Friday EOD (3/19).
[08:06] Evan: Good. Anything else?
[08:08] Olivia: One last question — how do you handle model rollbacks if a model variant underperforms? Is that manual?
[08:14] Priya: We have automated rollback hooks based on evaluation signals or manual. You can set A/B thresholds. Also, fallback policies to a smaller model if capacity issues occur.
[08:26] Carlos: For network latency debugging, do you provide any sample scripts or traceroutes to confirm path?
[08:31] Priya: Yes, we'll share a small diagnostics script you can run to capture RTTs and egress validation.
[08:38] Evan: Ok let's wrap with a quick recap. Jamie?
[08:40] Jamie: Recap: (1) Jamie sends runbook + security pack by 2026-03-19; (2) Priya posts allowlist and Terraform snippets by 2026-03-22; (3) Evan/Carlos share sample prompts and do firewall work by 2026-03-24; (4) schedule observability deep-dive for 2026-03-23. Pilot target window: week of 2026-03-29.
[09:02] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:05] Evan: Thanks.
[09:06] Priya: Thanks all, I'll follow up in the doc and chat.
[41:30] -- meeting ends --

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "KV cache" appears as "K V cash" in some auto text; team corrected inline.
